REST handlers are methods (get/post/put/delete) of flask_restx.Resource subclasses in mindsdb/api/http/namespaces/**; there is no standalone Decorator AST type, and routes are class-level @ns_conf.route(...) decorators, so source extraction keys on Resource-subclass methods and their parameters (path variables such as the file name in File.put(self, name: str), namespaces/file.py:33).

The most important external input surface is request.json (43 sites) - notably POST /api/sql/query (sql.py:29 query = request.json["query"]), POST /api/databases (databases.py:31 database = request.json['database'] with 'parameters' = handler connection args, including URL-bearing engines), and PUT /api/files/<name> with source_type == 'url' (file.py:92-116).

mindsdb also accepts SQL over wire protocols, not just HTTP: MysqlProxy.process_query(self, sql) (mindsdb/api/mysql/mysql_proxy/mysql_proxy.py:522, also inherited by FakeMysqlProxy used by the HTTP /api/sql/query endpoint, classes/fake_mysql_proxy/fake_mysql_proxy.py:14) and PostgresProxy.process_query(self, sql) (mindsdb/api/postgres/postgres_proxy/postgres_proxy.py:253). The Mongo wire server (mindsdb/api/mongo/server.py) translates BSON ops into the same SQL executor layer.

Auth: initialize.py:251-267 before_request returns 403 for protected namespaces when config['auth']['http_auth_enabled'] is True and check_auth() (default.py:28-36, session username or config user match) fails; when http_auth_enabled is False (common self-hosted default) the protected namespaces are unauthenticated. SQL executed through MySQL/Postgres wire protocols follows those protocols' own auth. Reachability is noted, not judged in this phase.

Integration handlers receive caller-controlled connection_data (dict) - from CREATE DATABASE ... project_identity: MindsDB (open-source AI-SQL platform): brings ML/LLM integrations to SQL. The application package mindsdb/ contains api/ (Flask REST API under api/http, plus MySQL/Postgres/Mongo wire-protocol servers), integrations/ (~200 handler packages under handlers/, handler libs, gRPC handler wrapper), interfaces/ (controllers for integrations, files, models, jobs, skills, ...), utilities/ (config, auth, telemetry) and migrations/.

Server-side network activity for CWE-918 is concentrated in: (a) the file ingestion path (files API 'source_type == url' upload, file_handler URL fetch, mysql executor download_file for PATH-type connection args), (b) the web crawl handler (SELECT ... FROM web WHERE url = ...), (c) per-integration handler API clients (fixed provider hosts or user-supplied url/host from connection args), (d) cloud/OAuth support code (config-controlled hosts).

notes: Extraction rules were derived only from repository evidence and the CWE-918 pass focus; no vulnerability ground truth, CVE descriptions, fix diffs, or pre-located vulnerable lines were consulted (pre-existing root-level analysis artifacts were deliberately not read).

Both extraction queries are plain multi-column select queries (no @kind metadata) for use with `codeql query run` + `codeql bqrs decode`; they are not intended for `codeql database analyze` SARIF output.

CSV column order matches the prior-project convention (calibre-web / fides): node, candidate_type, callable, flow_kind, receiver, moduleHint, arg_index, line, file:line, expression. arg_index is -1 when not applicable.
flow_kind vocabulary: param/return/field/argument as in prior projects.

AST-literal matching (requests.get by object Name 'requests', Resource base matched by class-base Name 'Resource', os.environ.get matched structurally) is used because CodeQL resolved-API modeling is not guaranteed for every optional dependency; every matched call-site family was individually confirmed against this source tree, and import resolution must be validated during LLM labeling.

Expected candidate volume (from grep counts, to be confirmed by query run): ~64 request-container attribute sources, ~35-45 Resource-method path-variable params, 2 process_query sql params, 2 env-var sources; ~83 requests.<verb> sink rows (64 get, 16 post, 1 put, 1 head, 1 delete; url= keyword variants counted separately), 9 requests.request rows, 1 session.get row.

urllib.request.urlopen / urlretrieve / httpx / aiohttp / http.client are NOT used anywhere in mindsdb/ (verified by grep; urllib usage is parse-only) - no candidates and no coverage gap for those APIs.

No file:/data: scheme fetching exists in this source tree (file_handler _get_file_path explicitly restricts to http/https; download_file rejects empty scheme); nothing extracted for non-HTTP schemes. Local-only file reads are not CWE-918 sinks and are not extracted.

Scope restriction path.matches("mindsdb/%") + not path.matches("mindsdb/%/tests/%") excludes the nested mindsdb-db CodeQL database directory, the repo-root tests/ tree and all per-handler tests/ directories by construction.

coverage_gaps: Jira SDK: jira_handler.py:54-61 creates requests.Session() and passes it to Jira(url=self.connection_data['jira_url'], session=s) - the HTTP requests to the jira_url happen inside the jira package (not in this database); the connection_data boundary is captured as a source-side family only via the generic request.json/SQL surfaces. Not extracted as a sink.

Other per-handler SDK-driven integrations that perform network I/O inside third-party packages (e.g. cloud SDKs, DB drivers) are invisible to taint tracking; only handlers whose own code calls requests.* are covered by the sink families.

requests.request(**kwargs) wrappers: lightdash_handler/api.py:21 and sap_erp_handler/api.py:55 pass the URL inside a kwargs dict, so the URL argument position is not extractable at the call site; extracted with arg index -1 - the URL-bearing parameter is the wrapper method's url/params argument (labeling must resolve it).

Mongo wire protocol: queries arrive as BSON operations at mindsdb/api/mongo/server.py (MongoRequestHandler, OpMsgResponder etc.) and are translated into the same SQL executor pipeline; there is no single sql parameter to extract, so this entry surface is documented rather than extracted.

Second-order (response-derived) URLs: urlcrawl_helpers.py:118-136 builds follow-up crawl URLs from href attributes read out of fetched pages (urljoin at :122) and crawls them recursively; response-to-URL propagation needs a summary step in Phase 2 if labeling considers it in-scope.

gRPC handler service boundary: in modular mode, ML handler calls and the executor service communicate over gRPC (handlers_wrapper, session_controller executor_url is http for delete only); intra-gRPC flows are not modeled.

Cloud/OAuth support code targets config-derived hosts (namespaces/auth.py, utilities/auth.py: server_host from Config) and fixed AWS metadata/S3 URLs (utilities/auth.py:19, utilities/functions.py:86, gui.py, initialize.py:71) - operator-configured or literal URLs, FP-leaning for CWE-918 per the workflow's 'admin-configured URLs -> FP' heuristic; extracted as sink candidates for completeness, weighting left to labeling.

file_handler._handle_source chunking uses langchain TextLoader/PyPDFLoader on already-downloaded local temp files - no network I/O; safe_extract/zipfile/tarfile extraction of uploaded archives is a path-traversal concern (Pass 1), not CWE-918.

Internal helper url parameters (download_file(url), _fetch_url(url: str), get_all_website_links(url), registry(url, ...)) are NOT extracted as sources - they are project-internal plumbing; the earliest untrusted boundaries (request.json/args/form/files/headers, Resource method path variables, process_query sql, env vars) are extracted instead, per the candidate strategy.
